item.title: Organizational Outcomes Through Event Leverage: A New Research Agenda for Sport Organizations
item.content:encoded:
Marijke Taks, University of Ottawa

Paul Hover, Mulier Institute

Koen Breedveld, The Hague University of Applied Sciences

Event leverage research has traditionally focused on economic and social impacts, but organizational outcomes within sport organizations remain understudied. This special issue establishes organizational outcomes—sustainable changes resulting from strategic event leveraging—as a distinct research domain, encompassing effectiveness, governance, partnerships, volunteer systems, learning, innovation, and financial sustainability.

The special issue shifts focus to sport organizations as primary units of analysis within the sport ecosystem. Rather than treating organizational benefits as incidental byproducts, the call positions them as explicit strategic objectives. This responds to demands from governments and funding agencies for evidence that publicly funded events generate meaningful, sustained public value.

Contributions should advance conceptual and methodological foundations by integrating organizational capacity and institutional theory frameworks. The special issue seeks empirical, theoretical, and conceptual papers using innovative methods such as longitudinal designs and mixed methods to improve measurement of organizational outcomes across different contexts.

Appel publié par European Sport Management Quarterly. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Organizational outcomes in sport events
  • Event leverage theory
  • Organizational effectiveness and efficiency
  • Strategic partnerships in sport
  • Volunteer recruitment and retention
  • Organizational learning and innovation
  • Organizational capacity development
  • Financial sustainability of sport organizations
  • Governance in sport organizations
  • Sport ecosystem and stakeholder networks
  • Methodological approaches to measuring organizational change
  • Sport event legacy and impact evaluation
  • Policy implications of organizational outcomes

Timeline

item.title: Global Trends, Homegrown Systems: Developing Global South-First Frameworks for Managing the Sport Ecosystem
item.content:encoded:
Sarthak Mondal, University of Portsmouth

Sahen Gupta, University of Portsmouth

Govindasamy Balasekaran, National Institute of Education, Singapore

Jo Clarke, Leeds Beckett University

The global sport industry has historically been shaped by theories and management approaches originating in the Global North, which often fail to account for the institutional, political, economic and cultural realities of sport in the Global South. This epistemic gap means that practitioners and policymakers in emerging economies lack conceptual tools tailored to their specific contexts, limiting the effectiveness of governance and development initiatives.

This special issue positions the Global South as a primary site of theoretical production and institutional innovation rather than merely a testing ground for Northern theories. Recent developments in cricket franchises, African football, Southeast Asian esports, and Gulf sport mega-events demonstrate distinctive governance and investment configurations that require bespoke analytical frameworks.

Appel publié par Managing Sport and Leisure. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Sport Economics, Policy and Governance Frameworks in Global South contexts, including financial sustainability, funding models, and policy transfer
  • Strategic Sport Leadership and Institutional Development in emerging economies
  • Technology, Innovation, Society and Culture in Sport, including data analytics and digital platforms
  • Emerging Trends in Sport Management such as esports, hybrid leagues, and athlete entrepreneurship
  • Multidisciplinary Integration in Sport Systems drawing on economics, sociology, psychology, and political science

Timeline

  • October 15, 2026: Abstract deadline
  • April 30, 2027: Manuscript deadline
